stitchTypes.value: Straight stitch only, single needle lockstitch, with reverse

needleSystem.value: DBx1, size 14 at delivery, range 9 to 18 on the base N (NA: DAx1 size 9 to 11; NH: DBx1 size 20 to 23, size 21 at delivery)

presserFootLift.value: 5.5 mm by hand, 13 mm by knee lifter (standard knee lift 10 mm, adjustable to a 13 mm maximum)

threadTrimmer.value: None on the base DDL-5550N; automatic thread trimmer on the DDL-5550N-7 only

feedSystem.value: Drop feed; max stitch length 5 mm; needle bar stroke 30.7 mm

motor.value: Not built in. Sold as a head; dealer bundles add a table, stand and a servo or clutch motor

frame.value: Cast industrial head; automatic lubricating full rotary hook; automatic lubrication with Juki New Defrix Oil No. 1

includedFeet.value: Dealer complete set: head, 48 x 20 in table with adjustable height (about 26 to 32 in), stand, servo motor, drawer, lamp, belt, tools, manual

stitchLengthMm.value: 5 on the base DDL-5550N and NH; 4 on the NA and the DDL-5550N-7

lubrication.value: Automatic, oil pan; Juki New Defrix Oil No. 1 (ISO VG7 equivalent)

claims: "Thread take-up mechanism, feed mechanism, thread paths and hook have been further improved to enhance responsiveness to material changes and to ensure consistent stitch quality" (Juki product page)
"Higher lift of the presser foot" (Juki product page)
"Sure thread trimming mechanism" (Juki product page, DDL-5550N-7)
Control box "resistant to voltage fluctuations, noise and vibration" (Juki product page, SC-920C)
"Suitable for light to medium-heavy materials" (dealer copy, GoldStar Tool)
"Runs quieter than traditional clutch motors" (dealer claim about the bundled servo motor, GoldStar Tool)
conflicts: Needle metric size: the Juki product page gives the size 14 as Nm75 for both the N and the N-7, while the Juki Americas catalog gives Nm75 for the -7 and Nm90 for the N; the DBx1 system and size 14 agree in both.

Weight: the Juki page lists a total weight of 81 kg in the DDL-5550N-7 table only, with no statement of what it includes, and one dealer snippet said about 75 lb for the head; neither is published as head weight, so weight stays [verify].
Speed and stitch length: 5,500 spm and 5 mm are the base DDL-5550N figures; the DDL-5550N-7 with trimmer is listed at 5,000 spm and 4 mm on the Juki page and catalog, and the NA and NH are 4,000 spm.
Throat: Juki publishes no arm space or throat figure for this model; one dealer lists a workspace of 10 1/4 in without saying what it is measured from, so throat stays [verify].
Country of manufacture: no Juki document fetched states it; Made in Japan rests on a Juki reply quoted in an Amazon Q&A and on dealer titles, so it is unverified and not published as fact.

Warranty: Juki publishes no model-specific warranty; Juki Americas lists a 90-day spare parts warranty and refers equipment to separate sales order terms, so the machine warranty is set by the selling dealer.

Model naming: the Juki page and catalog group the DDL-5550N, NA, NH and the -7 versions as one series, while Reddit threads often say DDL-5550-6 or N-7; no Juki document fetched separates a -6, so those threads are read as the same head family, not the exact model.

ownerThemes.theme: Owners who moved from a domestic machine say the oil pan means no oiling routine and the stitch is balanced and consistent; one paid about $900 for a complete set.
First-industrial buyers report they rarely touch the domestic machine afterward and wish they had bought sooner.
New owners ask about servo motor setup, speed control and bobbin winding while sewing; the long production run means parts and advice are easy to find.
DIY table bundles draw complaints about poor or missing assembly instructions; others found the included instructions adequate.

crossShop.why: The other Juki single-needle lockstitch sold to home shops; same 5,500 spm class, usually a little cheaper and not marketed as made in Japan.
Buyers sewing leather, vinyl or canvas find the drop-feed DDL is the wrong tool and step up to the walking foot machine.
The portable straight-stitch alternative for anyone without floor space for a 48 in industrial table.

editorial.verdict: A Juki industrial straight stitch head with a 13 mm knee lift and automatic oiling that needs a table, a motor and floor space, and whose throat, head weight and origin Juki does not publish.
editorial.whoFor: A home shop sewing garments, bags or quilts in volume who wants an industrial lockstitch with a long parts history and is willing to give up zigzag entirely.
editorial.skipIf: You sew grippy or very thick stacks such as leather, rubber sheet or many layers of webbing (owners report failures there), or you have no room for a 48 by 20 in table.
editorial.keySpec: 5,500 spm and 5 mm on the base N · 13 mm knee lift · DBx1 needle
strengths: Automatic lubrication with an oil pan: an owner on PatternReview reports upkeep is mostly cleaning lint.
Juki publishes a 13 mm maximum knee lift and 5.5 mm hand lift, and a 5 mm stitch length on the base N.
Owners report second-hand units running well after basic fixes, and a long production run means parts and advice are easy to find.
weaknesses: Owners report trouble on thick stacks: needle breaks on 3 layers of heavy webbing, and failures on 6 or more layers of duck.
Owner reports on reliability are mixed, from a unit that ran about 20 years before its power board failed to a bundle delivered with broken parts; some report oil leaks from the pan.
Juki publishes no throat figure, head weight, country of origin or model-specific warranty, so those rows read [verify].

checks.title: Which suffix the listing ships
checks.body: Speed and stitch length differ by version: 5,500 spm and 5 mm on the base N, 5,000 spm and 4 mm on the N-7 with trimmer, 4,000 spm on the NA and NH. Confirm which one the listing ships.

checks.title: Servo or clutch motor
checks.body: Juki sells the head and lists a servomotor and control box with the -7; the older manual names a 400 W clutch motor. One owner finds the clutch motor on the N very loud, so check which motor the bundle includes.

checks.body: The Amazon listing B08H8TYNW1 is a DDL-5550 DIY bundle rated 3.4 from 10 ratings, and one buyer there received broken parts. Check what ships, who assembles it, and the dealer's warranty terms.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki DDL-5550 and DDL-5550N?
faqs.a: Juki lists the DDL-5550N, NA, NH and the -7 trimmer versions as one series, and dealers mix the DDL-5550 and DDL-5550N names. The NA is the light-weight setup, the NH the heavy-weight setup, and the -7 adds an automatic thread trimmer.
Reddit owners often say DDL-5550-6, but no Juki document we fetched separates a -6 version. We treat those threads as the same head family, not the exact model.

faqs.q: How fast does the DDL-5550N sew?
faqs.a: Juki lists 5,500 stitches per minute for the base DDL-5550N, 5,000 for the -7 with trimmer and 4,000 for the NA and NH. A servo motor lets you sew slower.

faqs.q: Does the DDL-5550 have an automatic thread trimmer?
faqs.a: Not on the base DDL-5550N. Juki lists only the DDL-5550N-7 as the version with an automatic thread trimmer, at 5,000 spm and 4 mm stitch length.
DBx1 needles. The base N ships with a size 14 and takes sizes 9 to 18. The Juki page and catalog disagree on the metric equivalent of size 14, Nm75 against Nm90, so check the needle packet.

faqs.q: Does it come with a motor?
faqs.a: Juki lists the head with a servomotor and control box on the -7, and an older manual names a 400 W clutch motor as standard. Dealer bundles add a table, stand and motor, so check the listing.
[verify]. Juki lists 81 kg total weight in the -7 table without saying what it includes, and one dealer snippet said about 75 lb for the head. Neither is a confirmed head weight.

faqs.q: How much room is there to the right of the needle?
faqs.a: [verify]. Juki publishes no arm space or throat figure for this model. One dealer lists a 10 1/4 in workspace without saying how it is measured.

faqs.q: Is the DDL-5550 made in Japan?
faqs.a: Unverified. No Juki document we fetched states the country of manufacture. A Juki reply quoted in an Amazon Q&A and dealer titles say Made in Japan, but we do not publish it as fact.
